ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher refund of $2.76 (RydeTAXI metered mileage overcharge for the unexempt 18:46–18:52 segment) to the rider; record the RD-1 breach against the driver in the trip file; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so distance driven enters the fare directly and an unexempt deviation is refundable in mileage units [F6][F4][RD-2][RD-1]. The record sets one off-route segment, 18:46–18:52, 3.50 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.54 km, +1.96 km and up to 752 m off the optimal route [F3][RD-1].

RD-4(a) is settled against the driver by the trace: the only incident record is a vehicle breakdown reported 18:27 on the East Coast Parkway at 0 m from the optimal route [F11][F3], but that report predates the segment start by 19 min and the trace records no qualifying incident covering the replaced stretch; the surviving traffic records are speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on ECP and Airport Boulevard, which are not bands 1–2 and cannot exempt a segment on their own [F9][F10][RD-4][RD-4(b)]. The driver's post-trip statement that "the whole road was slow, so I took another way" is a claim of cause, not evidence of cause or of consent [F8][RD-4][RD-5].

RD-5 consent fails on the record: there are no in-app chat messages at all between rider and driver [F7][F3], so no rider message sent before 18:46:55 agrees to this segment, whether generally or as a named road; a driver's statement of agreement is not consent [F8][RD-5][G11]. The segment therefore counts as an unexempt deviation, and RD-3 does not apply because no stop is measured in the segment [F3][RD-3(a)].

Amount: this trip's rate is distance fare ÷ distance km = $33.33 ÷ 23.64 km = $1.4099/km [F6][F4][RD-2]. The unexempt segment's extra_km is 1.96 km [F3], so the refund is 1.96 km × $1.4099/km = $2.7634 → $2.76 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The remainder of the billed excess line (2.17 km, $3.06) is corridor/matching mileage not attributable to any segment and is not refundable under RD-2 [F4][F3][RD-2]; surge was 1.0×, waiting fee $0.00 and the platform fee $1.47 is published, so there is no further FARE-1 exposure [F5][F6][FARE-1].

Profile facts do not decide the case: the driver has 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days and the rider has no history [F13][F14][RD-6]. The trace settles RD-6 as ✗, so no account flag is added even though the RD-2 refund is positive [F14][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The chat record contains no in-app messages at all, so there is no rider message sent before the segment start (18:46:55) agreeing to this route [F7]; the driver's post-trip statement that he 'took another way' is a statement, not rider consent [F8][RD-5][G11]. The segment's 1.96 km extra is therefore not exempt and is refundable under RD-2 [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The +2.1 km / +10% whole-trip figure is not the refundable measure: RD-1/RD-2 require segment-by-segment assessment, and only the 18:46–18:52 segment's 1.96 km is unexempt [F1][F3][F4][RD-1][RD-2].

Accepted as to measurement (one segment, +1.96 km, up to 752 m off route [F3]) but the characterisation of it as unexplained is not adopted: the incident/band records are examined and rejected as an exemption on timing and band grounds, not treated as absent [F3][F9][F10][F11][RD-4].

The $3.06 excess-distance line is computed over the whole 2.17 km excess, part of which is corridor/matching mileage not attributable to any segment; RD-2 refunds only the unexempt segment's extra_km, i.e. 1.96 km × $1.4099/km = $2.76 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].
Correctly states RD-6 is not met; likewise adopted here — 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days, so no flag_account [F14][RD-6].

Agreed that the corridor/matching remainder is not refundable under RD-2, but the driver's claim that RD-2 leaves nothing payable is rejected: the single segment is unexempt under RD-4/RD-5 [F3][F4][F9][F10][F11][RD-2][RD-4][RD-5].

RD-4(a) is settled ✗ by the trace: the breakdown was reported 18:27, 19 minutes before the segment began at 18:46, and does not qualify as an incident covering the replaced stretch, even though it sits 0 m from the optimal route [F11][F3][RD-4].

Speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on ECP and Airport Boulevard is not band 1 or 2 and cannot exempt a segment standing alone; the driver's post-trip statement does not corroborate cause as consent cannot arise from it [F9][F10][F8][RD-4(b)][RD-5].
Correctly concedes no RD-5 consent exists — the chat is empty; this is exactly why the segment remains unexempt, as the RD-4 defence fails [F7][F3][RD-5][RD-4].
Correctly states no flag_account is warranted; the positive RD-2 refund does not trigger RD-6 because route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F14][RD-6].
